summary: Iteration 37: Backend + frontend validation of SaaS System Admin Panel (/api/system/*, /api/license/*) and Inbound e-Document Inbox (/api/edocs/inbox/*). All 24 pytest cases pass (100%). Frontend: super-admin login shows license-badge 'Kurumsal · Aktif', nav-item-sistem + nav-item-edoc-inbox visible; /sistem renders all 5 tabs with expected data-testids (stat-companies/stat-mrr, company-row-*, new-company-btn, new-plan-btn, saas-module-catalog, saas-requests). Company drawer opens via company-manage-{id} button; disabling /ecommerce hides the sidebar item and shows module-locked panel with upgrade CTA; re-enabling restores both. /settings?tab=plan renders my-plan-panel (name+status), 20 my-module cards, 4 plan-card cards, billing-y toggle, and plan-request-plan_pro button. /edoc-inbox renders page, upload input and status filters. Non-super-admin (satis@nexus.com): 'Sistem Yönetimi' is hidden and direct visit shows system-denied panel; /api/system/overview returns 403.
critical_code_review_comments: CompaniesTable rows use a dedicated 'Yönet' button (data-testid=company-manage-{id}) to open the license drawer; the row (company-row-{id}) itself is NOT clickable. Task spec implies clicking the row opens the drawer — consider adding an onClick to the row OR update the spec/doc so testers know to use the manage button. This tripped the initial UI test.

GET /api/system/plans, /system/companies, /system/modules, /system/upgrade-requests return raw JSON arrays (not wrapped). Consider a consistent {items:[...]} envelope for pagination/metadata later, but current shape is fine.

saas.effective() returns license fields at the top level (plan_id, plan_name, status, modules, module_overrides, ...) plus catalog/plans/users/pending_request. Frontend appears to consume this shape directly — good.
edocs.list_inbox returns {items:[...], counts:{...}} which is nicely wrapped; recommend applying the same envelope to /system/* endpoints for consistency.
